verdict: The accepted version keeps all DFT results, figures 2-5 and the XRD analysis, and adds three short pieces of evidence: cross-sectional STEM shown as qualitative support for intercalation, a statement that several samples reproduce the 170 T peak, and one Hall carrier density. The theory section gains sentences on Ru magnetism, strain and the limited parameter range, without new calculations. The title drops 'new' and the Conclusions become conditional on spectroscopic and magnetic validation. The changes point to referees who asked for more structural evidence, reproducibility, Hall data and a more cautious outlook, and who accepted text answers on the theory. Many of the old review's numerical concerns (distances, FFT labels, controls, novelty against ref. 27) are left untouched.

inferred_requests.title: Give direct structural evidence that α-RuCl3 is intercalated
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely found the XRD-by-analogy argument too thin and asked for direct real-space or compositional evidence of intercalation and layering. The authors added cross-sectional STEM, which they present as qualitative.

inferred_requests.title: Show the oscillations are reproducible across samples
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked whether the SdH frequencies recur in other pieces and other growths. The authors report a second piece of the S2 crystal and multiple independent samples with the same 170 T peak.

inferred_requests.title: Report the Hall data and carrier density
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked for the Hall measurement mentioned in Methods, to give carrier type and density. One density value was added to the results and the Hall effect to the Conclusions.

inferred_requests.title: Justify the Fermi-level shift used to match DFT to SdH
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely questioned the freedom of an ad hoc 0.1 eV shift in matching computed pockets to measured frequencies. The authors added a sentence saying only a limited parameter range works and softened the stacking-fault statement.

inferred_requests.title: Address the magnetism of the intercalated RuCl3 layers
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked whether the RuCl3 layers stay magnetic, and how non-magnetic DFT and strain affect this. The authors added assertions that Ru keeps its magnetic nature and that strain may affect magnetism, without new calculations or measurements.

inferred_requests.title: Tone down the exotic-phase framing
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely said that no measurement supports correlated, topological or magnetic phases. The authors dropped 'new' from the title and made the outlook conditional on spectroscopic and magnetic validation; the abstract is unchanged.

inferred_requests.title: Rule out mixed staging or disorder
inferred_requests.text: Referees likely asked whether samples are single-stage and ordered, given only 00l XRD and visible residual graphite. The authors argue that mixed staging would broaden the oscillation spectrum, which is not observed.

inferred_requests.title: Deposit the data
inferred_requests.text: Data now sit in a public repository. This may be journal policy rather than a referee request.

inferred_requests.title: Add a schematic of charge transfer and band evolution
inferred_requests.text: A new Fig. 1f illustrates charge transfer and ABC band evolution. This could be a referee's request for a clearer overview or an editorial addition.

inferred_requests.title: Fix typos and cross-references
inferred_requests.text: Some typos were fixed and SI pointers made specific; several typos flagged earlier remain. Likely copy-editing rather than referees.

issue_status.reason: STEM adds qualitative evidence of layered intercalation, but no composition, oxidation state, Raman or Ag check is reported.
A Hall density and multi-sample reproducibility were added, but no LK masses, angle dependence, Dingle analysis or explicit pocket assignment.
Calculations remain non-spin-polarized GGA; only an assertion that Ru keeps its magnetic nature was added.
STEM shows alternating contrast and a mixed-staging argument was added, but stacking still rests on assumptions and no l≠0 data appear.
The same fixed distances (3.60, 3.54 Å) are used and no tabulation against the measured c-axis periods is given; SI changes cannot be seen.
Title drops 'new' and the Conclusions add a validation caveat, but the abstract keeps the strong framing and no magnetic data were added.
'For the first time' remains and ref. 27 is not discussed.
Controls are unchanged: Cl2-annealed Kish graphite in ρ(T) only.
Multiple samples are said to reproduce the 170 T peak, but no counts, spread or stage-4 ρ(T) are given.
FFT procedure and harmonic labels (359, 347 T) are unchanged.
The main text still quotes ≈4% strain; the SI is not available to check normalizations.
Contour method and 'small systematic error' unchanged; dhva cross-check still A|A only.
'heretostructures' and 'of of' fixed, but 'α-Cul3', '29.5(A)' and 'hdva' remain.
No change to units or dimensions in Fig. 2.
RRR still defined at 2 K and no values listed.
The Cl2-annealed control is still not discussed quantitatively.
Stacking notation and the cross-RuCl3 registry justification are unchanged.
0.68 and 0.48 eV still quoted without naming the cell; SI not visible.
The Introduction is unchanged, but the Conclusions now make the flat-band link conditional on validation.
The Fig. 1 caption still does not mark A|A as a reference model.
Methods on k-mesh and D3 are unchanged.
Data are now in a public repository with a DOI.
